fundamental.thesis: Larsen & Toubro is India's largest engineering and construction (EPC) company, with additional arms in manufacturing, tech services and financial services, and it holds a record order book of ₹853,514 cr, about 3.0x annual revenue and up 15% since March 2026. In H1 FY27 revenue rose 11.4% YoY to ₹146,692 cr and PAT rose 23.6% to ₹9,325 cr. Subtracting Q1 (₹67,942 cr revenue, ₹4,123 cr PAT, +6.7% and +14% YoY) gives an implied Q2 of about ₹78,750 cr revenue (about +16% YoY) and ₹5,202 cr PAT (about +32%), so growth actually picked up in Q2. The pre-computed 'decelerating' signal compares H1 numbers against single quarters and is misleading, and order inflow grew 22% YoY to ₹255,678 cr. The weak spot is operating quality: EBITDA margin fell from 10.0% to 8.8% YoY, with Infrastructure margin down 50bps to 5.4% and Energy-Conventional down 40bps to 7.6%, and cash conversion is thin at 0.62x CFO/PAT. On the card's EV/EBITDA plus order-cover yardstick, 18.4x EV/EBITDA is 46% below the Industrials median of 34x, and trailing P/E of 35.6x sits mid-band in the 28–45x sector range. The large peer discount mostly reflects the structurally lower margins of EPC versus richly priced electricals like ABB and CGPOWER, so I grade it fair rather than cheap, with the stock at 76% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that EBITDA margins keep falling while revenue accelerates on a 54%-international, aggressively bid order book, at a time when the sector de-rates on any capex-pause fear and macro conditions are risk-off.

fundamental.thesis: ITC is a diversified Indian conglomerate where the cigarettes franchise (~70% of operating profit) funds FMCG Others (branded packaged goods), Agri Business, Paper & Packaging, and Hotels — it is priced on a structural conglomerate discount rather than as a pure FMCG compounder, and the sector card explicitly names it 'its own animal.' Q1FY27 revenue of ₹29,523 cr shows a misleading +27.6% YoY surge driven almost entirely by excise duty reclassification post GST-compensation-cess expiry (Feb 2026), where cigarette excise surged 538% to ₹10,409 cr; the underlying picture is PAT down -15.6% YoY to ₹4,509 cr (including an exceptional ₹406 cr Sproutlife gain) with EBITDA margin compressed sharply from 32.7% to 20.0% — this follows a weak multi-year trajectory of FY26 PAT +1.0%, FY25 PAT -0.8%, and CFO/PAT deteriorating to 0.59× in H1FY26 (below the 0.6 warning threshold), signalling earnings stagnation and weakening cash conversion. On P/E, ITC at 16.93× sits at P0 (cheapest in sector) vs a peer median of 51.5× and the 40–65× FMCG benchmark, and is equally at the floor on EV/EBITDA (12.1× vs peer median 34.6×) and P/B — the valuation case is unambiguous on any yardstick, but the discount is structural (tobacco overhang, conglomerate penalty, no near-term demerger catalyst) and a re-rating requires either a sustained PAT recovery or a structural unlock that is not yet visible. The biggest risk is that the cess-expiry margin compression is permanent — the street is still repricing this, with sell-side EPS estimates cut -8.8% over 90 days — making the cheap multiple a value trap until a clear earnings inflection quarter arrives.

Bajaj Finance is India's largest diversified retail NBFC, with AUM of ₹5.85L cr (+26% YoY) and a franchise of 129 million customers across consumer, SME, mortgage, gold and microfinance loans. In Q2FY27, net total income was ₹15,974 cr (+23% YoY) and PAT was ₹6,367 cr (+29% YoY). AUM growth has sped up from +22% to +24% to +26% over three quarters, ROE is 20.6%, and GNPA improved year on year from 1.24% to 1.06%. However, GNPA rose from 0.96% in Q1, and Stage 2+3 loans climbed from 1.87% to 2.02% as the gold-loan book moves through its early stages. For a lender the right valuation measure is price-to-book against ROE, not P/E. On that basis the stock is expensive: 4.9x book against a sustainable ROE of about 19-21%, the highest in its peer group (P100, +62% over the 3.0x median), with trailing P/E of 29.6x against a peer median of 20.1x. Growth delivery is excellent, but the price already reflects much of it, and the sell-side gave the stock no upward estimate revisions in the last 30 days (-0.5%). The biggest risks are funding costs and dilution. Management itself expects up to two more repo hikes to 6% while cost of funds is already 7.31%, which works against a lender in a RISK_OFF market where Financials are underweight. On top of that, the ₹11,700 cr QIP plus ₹5,800 cr of promoter warrants will dilute existing shareholders by about 3%.

fundamental.thesis: Hexaware is a mid-tier IT services company owned by Carlyle. Most of its revenue comes from the US and Europe, and its fastest-growing segments are Healthcare & Insurance and Manufacturing. In the latest indexed quarter (Q2 CY26, June), revenue rose 17.9% YoY to Rs 3,845 cr, but only 6.3% in constant currency, so most of the headline growth came from the weak rupee. Constant-currency growth did improve from 3.2% the quarter before. PAT fell 13% YoY to Rs 330 cr, and PAT margin has shrunk from 10.6% to 8.6% over the trend window, even though EBIT margin rose 68 bps QoQ to 13.6%. On valuation, the trailing P/E of 21.8x (forward 18.2x) is just below the 22-30x IT benchmark, and EV/EBITDA of 13.0x looks modest. I grade it fair rather than cheap because the peer comparison is against the whole market, not IT peers, and analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 6.1% over 90 days. The stock sits at 18.6% of its 52-week range. Two big caveats: results for the September quarter were due at the 28-Oct board meeting and are not in this data, so the figures may be stale; and a 14.5% fall in Travel & Transportation plus falling PAT are the main fundamental risks.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Unilever is India's largest FMCG company, with leading positions in soaps, detergents, personal care and foods. The latest results we have extracted are Q1FY27 (the Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-10-28 are not yet in the trend table). In Q1FY27, revenue grew 10.1% YoY to ₹17,341 cr, up from about 5% in FY26 and about 2% in FY25. Underlying volume growth rose from 4% in FY26 to 6% in Q4FY26, ahead of price/mix at 2%, which is the healthy way to grow. Profit lagged, though: PAT fell 3.2% YoY to ₹2,680 cr and PAT margin was 15.5%; earlier periods' margins (51% in Q3FY25, 41% PAT growth in FY26) look distorted by one-off gains. On valuation, the stock trades at 46.6x trailing and 39.4x forward earnings, inside the usual 40–60x FMCG range. Against its peers it sits in the middle on P/E (60th percentile) and toward the pricey end on EV/EBITDA (80th percentile), so 'fair' is our grade. The price is near the bottom of its 52-week range, which helps entry. The biggest risk is that crude above $100 pushes up input costs and keeps profit growth behind sales growth, and we cannot confirm the trend until the Q2 filing is extracted. Several live data points are clearly wrong and were not used: a 212% dividend yield, debt/equity of 3.0 (HUL is a net-cash company), and an analyst target that doesn't match the 52-week price range.

fundamental.thesis: Axis Bank is India's third-largest private-sector bank, with a large corporate and wholesale book, a growing retail franchise and a consolidated life-insurance associate (Axis Max Life). In Q2FY27, total income rose 14.8% YoY to ₹45,674 cr and PAT rose 39.4% to ₹7,705 cr. Revenue growth has picked up from about +4% (H1FY26) to +7% (Q1FY27) to +15%, and loan growth has risen from 11.9% to 19.3%, but the PAT jump is flattered by a weak Q2FY26 base (₹5,528 cr), and the PAT margin slipped from 17.7% in Q1 to 16.9%. On the lender yardstick from the sector card (P/B against sustainable ROE), a P/B of 1.83x for a TTM ROE of 13.2% is fair: it is above the peer median of 1.5x (P64), while trailing P/E of 15.0x is about 11% below peers (P43). That fits a bank whose asset quality has improved (GNPA down from 1.46% to 1.23%) but whose returns are only moderate. The biggest risk is that loans are now growing faster than deposits: the loan-to-deposit ratio is a stretched 98.7%, credit cost has risen from 0.20% to 0.72%, and provision coverage is slipping (70.5% to 70.0%). Together these point to future funding-cost and NIM pressure, and the extracted NIM readings (3.42% in Q1 vs 2.32% in Q2) conflict too much to confirm the NIM recovery the sector card expects.

fundamental.thesis: Sun Pharma is India's largest drugmaker. It holds about 8.5% of the India formulations market (No. 1), and its global specialty (Innovative Medicines) business now makes up about 22% of sales, so its growth no longer depends mainly on US generics. In Q1FY27 revenue rose 10.1% YoY to ₹15,184 cr and reported PAT rose 26.9% to ₹2,895 cr, a 19.1% margin. Some of the PAT jump comes from the lower tax rate it moved to, and it is despite ₹204 cr of one-off Organon and labour-code charges. Underneath, the business is weaker: EBITDA grew only 2.7%, the EBITDA margin fell to 28.9% from about 31-32% in FY26, India grew 16% but US formulations shrank 9.7% in USD as lenalidomide competition hits, and the trend table mixes quarterly, half-year and nine-month figures, so the 'accelerating' revenue signal is not reliable. On valuation, a trailing P/E of 37.4x sits inside the 28-40x pharma range and near the peer median (P54), while EV/EBITDA of 24.2x is 13% above the peer median (P62); judged on P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers, the stock is fairly valued, with only modest support from the 27.7x forward P/E and slightly rising estimates. The biggest risk is the $11.75B Organon acquisition: closing it in Q4FY27 turns a net-cash balance sheet (about ₹26,000 cr of net cash in FY25, FY26 debt/equity 0.05) into a leveraged one with integration risk. fundamental.thesis: UltraTech is India's largest cement maker with 210.1 mtpa of capacity, and it benefits from an industry where it and Adani now control roughly 45% of capacity, which supports pricing discipline. In Q2FY27 revenue grew 18.9% YoY to ₹23,024 cr, up from 15.8% in Q1, and PAT rose 21.3% to ₹1,501 cr on 12.9% volume growth. Margins fell sharply from Q1, though: EBITDA margin dropped from 20.9% to 16.6% and PAT margin from 10.6% to 6.5%, and EBITDA per tonne fell from ₹1,214 to ₹974 (still up ₹60 YoY). The cause is cost inflation, with fuel up 14% and packing bags up 30% on the crude spike, against realisation growth of only 2%. Part of this is the normal monsoon-quarter slowdown, and H1 cash conversion is solid at 1.68x CFO/PAT. Using the cement yardstick (EBITDA per tonne plus peer multiples, since live EV/EBITDA was not available), the stock looks fair. Its 39.6x trailing P/E is close to the sector median of 37.3x (P53 among peers), but the 4.5x P/B is rich for a 10.6% ROE, and the 25.1x forward P/E rests on estimates that have been cut 11–13% in the last 30 days. The biggest risk is that crude above $103 keeps fuel and packing costs high while realisations barely rise, so per-tonne profits stay squeezed and the stock de-rates as analysts keep trimming earnings.

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Finserv is a financial holding company whose value comes mainly from its stake in Bajaj Finance, India's largest consumer lender, plus its life and general insurance subsidiaries and newer AMC, health and broking businesses. In Q1 FY27, consolidated total income grew 19.2% YoY to ₹42,037 cr, up from +12.6% a year earlier. However, PAT attributable to owners grew only 12% to ₹3,132 cr, which works out to a margin of about 7.5% versus 7.9% in Q1 FY26. The 'expanding margin' trajectory signal is an artifact: the ₹6,297 cr headline figure includes minority shareholders, while the prior-year figures in the table appear to be attributable-only. Within the group, Bajaj Finance is strong (PAT +28%, AUM +24%, Gross NPA down to 0.96% from 1.24%, provision coverage up to 60%), Bajaj Life VNB rose 87%, but Bajaj General's PAT fell 27% as its combined ratio worsened to 104.7%. On the lender yardstick the sector card prescribes (P/B against sustainable ROE), a P/B of 3.5x for an ROE of 14.6% is a premium (P73 vs peers, sector median P/B 2.0x). That is partly justified by the quality of Bajaj Finance and offset by the stock sitting at only 21% of its 52-week range, so I grade it fair rather than cheap. The biggest near-term swing factor is Q2 FY27 results on 3 Nov 2026, eight days away, where continued general-insurance underwriting losses and cash burn in the emerging businesses could drag on owner-level earnings growth.

NTPC is India's largest power generator and earns a regulated return of about 15.5% on the plants it commissions, so its profits grow with how much new capacity it adds rather than with power prices. In Q1FY27 (consolidated), revenue was ₹51,142 cr, up 7.0% YoY, and PAT was ₹6,896 cr, up 12.9%, for a 13.6% PAT margin, compared with -4.2% revenue growth and an 11.2% margin in Q1FY26. The pre-computed 'accelerating' and 'expanding' trend signals are not reliable, because the table mixes single quarters with half-year and nine-month totals; only the two Q1 figures can be fairly compared. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and P/B with ROE, the right measures for a capital-heavy regulated utility: EV/EBITDA of 8.4x is the cheapest in its sector and 28% below the 11.6x peer median, P/B is 1.7x against a 13.7% ROE, and trailing P/E of 11.9x sits at the low end of the 10–18x sector range. That makes it cheap against peers but only modestly cheap in absolute terms, and the forward P/E (12.8x) being above the trailing P/E suggests flat near-term earnings. The biggest risk is that Q2FY27 results come out on 31 Oct and will replace these numbers, while high leverage and a ₹12,000 cr NCD borrowing plan keep the stock dependent on interest rates and on the next CERC review of the allowed return.

fundamental.thesis: Power Grid Corporation is India's dominant inter-state transmission utility, earning a regulated ROE (~15.5%) on an expanding fixed-asset base — a classic annuity where earnings growth equals capex commissioned rather than tariff or volume swings. Revenue grew a modest +2.7% YoY to ₹11,497 cr in Q1FY27, but PAT declined -0.9% YoY to ₹3,598 cr with PAT margin compressing from 34.7% in FY25 to 31.3% in Q1FY27; the core transmission segment (80% of revenue) delivered only +2.2% growth, suggesting asset commissioning pace has slowed even as consultancy revenue surged +27.75% YoY. Star Health is India's largest standalone health insurer: its health segment grew about 13% to ₹9,635 cr in H1 FY27, and it sells mostly retail policies through agents. H1 FY27 revenue rose 10.4% to ₹10,856 cr and PAT rose 57.3% to ₹815 cr, but Q2 alone was much weaker: taking H1 minus Q1 gives about ₹5,939 cr revenue and ₹265 cr PAT. That puts Q2 PAT margin near 4.5%, down from 11.2% in Q1, and revenue growth appears to have slowed from +13.4% to roughly +8%. The 'accelerating' flag compares periods of different lengths (half-year, quarter, full year, nine months), and the move to Ind AS this year restated the past figures, so the growth trend is noisy. For an insurer I grade on P/B against ROE rather than P/E: P/B of 3.3x with TTM ROE of only 7.5% (FY26 return on net worth 9.2%) is expensive under the desk rule (P/B above 3 with ROE below 12%). The 50.5x trailing P/E is not the right measure here, and the 20.4x forward P/E only holds up if the expected profit recovery actually arrives. The main risks are weaker underwriting and thinner capital: the combined operating ratio worsened from 92.3% to 94.5%, the claims ratio is stuck near 69%, cash from operations fell 54% (CFO/PAT 0.75x), and the FY26 solvency ratio of 1.63 is close to IRDAI's 1.5 minimum.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Enterprises is the Adani group's incubator. It runs airports, roads, data centres, mining services, copper and new-energy manufacturing, and it is valued on its capital-hungry project pipeline more than on current profits. Revenue growth sped up sharply: first-half FY27 revenue was ₹70,140 cr, up 62.3% YoY, against a 10.1% decline a year earlier. Second-quarter revenue, worked out as the H1 total minus Q1, was about ₹36,594 cr, up roughly 76% YoY. But copper (₹25,483 cr in H1, up about 12x) drove most of that growth and earns thin margins, while roads fell 68.7%. H1 PAT swung to a ₹241 cr loss from a ₹4,391 cr profit, mainly because of the ₹2,644 cr OFAC settlement, and finance costs rose 46% to ₹4,782 cr. Q2 PAT of about ₹919 cr gives a margin of only about 2.5%, versus 9.9% in FY26. The peer table compares the stock with Energy names like the oil marketing companies, which is the wrong comparison set, so I used EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for capital-intensive businesses. At 36.5x EV/EBITDA, with forward P/E (53.6x) above trailing P/E (41.1x), P/B of 4.8x on 13.7% ROE, and the price at 98.5% of its 52-week range, the stock is expensive for a business with negative free cash flow. The biggest risk is funding: H1 free cash flow was -₹10,800 cr and debt/equity is about 1.2, so the company relies on raising capital, as with the recent ₹15,000 cr QIP and the rights issue. Analysts also cut next-year EPS estimates by 14.7% in the last 30 days.

fundamental.thesis: Coal India is the state-owned near-monopoly supplier of domestic thermal coal, which makes its earnings a steady volume plus e-auction-premium annuity backed by a large dividend payout. H1 FY27 revenue rose 13.8% YoY to ₹90,434 cr and PAT rose 18.9% to ₹15,397 cr (17.0% PAT margin, 28.5% EBITDA margin), with operating cash flow at 2.21× PAT. The main risk is acquisition-driven leverage (net debt ₹49,686 cr, 1.86x EBITDA, current ratio 0.78) in a risk-off market with weak EM capital flows.

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Auto is one of India's leading two- and three-wheeler makers, with a large export business, a profitable EV arm (Chetak and electric 3-wheelers), and, from November 2025, a controlling stake in KTM. fundamental.thesis: Grasim Industries is an Aditya Birla Group conglomerate with dominant positions in cement (via UltraTech, India's largest producer), cellulosic fibres, caustic soda chemicals, and the rapidly-scaling Birla Opus paints venture — a multi-business platform that adds diversification but also cross-cycle complexity. Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew 21% YoY to ₹48,716 cr, accelerating from +16% in Q1FY26, while adjusted PAT surged 49% YoY to ₹2,153 cr; PAT margin expanded to 4.4% from 3.5% a year ago, underpinned by a highest-ever EBITDA of ₹8,077 cr (+26% YoY), 12.2% YoY cement volume growth (41.3 MT), and Birla Opus revenue up 64% YoY — all trajectory signals pointing upward. Using EV/EBITDA — the sector card's mandated yardstick for a capital-intensive conglomerate — Grasim trades at 13.25×, a 25.9% discount to the sector median 17.9× (P27 in sector, near cheapest quartile); the trailing P/E of 42.4× is inflated by Birla Opus's investment-phase PAT drag, and the forward P/E collapsing to 21.2× signals meaningful earnings normalization ahead, supported by analyst EPS upgrades of +8.6% over 30 days and a uniform 10/10 buy consensus — grade: fair, with a lean toward cheap on EV/EBITDA. The single largest risk is extreme consolidated debt/equity (134×), which includes ABCL's financial-services borrowings and UltraTech's cement-expansion debt, creating substantial interest-cost sensitivity in a rising-rate, RISK_OFF macro environment where FII flows are deeply negative and crude is pushing higher.

Asian Paints is India's largest decorative paints company, a consumer franchise with a growing industrial coatings and international arm, but its market leadership is under structural attack from Birla Opus. Growth has picked up sharply from +3-5% through FY26, but it is price-led: decorative volume grew +6.4% against value growth of +14.5%. Q2 PAT of about ₹1,086 cr grew only around 11% YoY, slowing sharply from +40% in Q1. Q2 consolidated EBITDA (PBDIT) margin fell 202 bps to 15.6% because of raw material inflation, and cash conversion weakened to 0.72x CFO/PAT in H1 from 1.66x a year ago. I graded valuation with the consumer-franchise P/E yardstick (30-60x) from the sector card, not steel or cement multiples. On that basis, a trailing P/E of 58.9x (forward 45.4x, EV/EBITDA 38x) is fair but at the top of the band. The P100 peer rank is inflated by commodity peers in the Materials group, and BERGEPAINT/PIDILITIND trade richer. The biggest risk is that crude above $100 and still rising, plus a weak rupee, keeps pushing input costs up while competition limits how much price the company can pass on, so margins could compress further.

fundamental.thesis: Britannia Industries is India's dominant biscuits and bakery company (leading share in cookies, rusks, bread, and dairy) — a defensive FMCG compounder where P/E against the 40-65× sector norm is the correct valuation yardstick, not EV/EBITDA. H1FY27 gross premium income accelerated to +16.2% YoY (₹39,734 cr) and PAT grew +13.7% to ₹1,133 cr — a clear improvement from FY26's +5.6% PAT growth — driven by retail protection (+42% YoY) and renewal premium growth (+15%), though embedded value VNB growth in 9MFY26 lagged at only +7% as VNB margin compressed to 24.4% from 25.1% prior year. The sector card prescribes P/EV as the primary yardstick for life insurers, but the extracted embedded value figure (₹615 cr) is implausibly low against a ₹1.2L cr market cap and cannot be reliably used; on peer-relative forward P/E (46x, P50 in the Insurance – Life peer set), HDFCLIFE is fairly valued, though P/B of 6.85x against ROE of only 11.3% is stretched, and the stock's position at 11% of its 52-week range offers a modestly improved entry. The biggest risk is crude above $100 and rising, which is a strong headwind for this name. With retail fuel prices sticky and a weak rupee, marketing losses can keep wiping out record refining margins, and interest costs are already up 57% and working-capital borrowing is building.

fundamental.thesis: Eternal (formerly Zomato) runs India's leading food-delivery platform plus Blinkit, the quick-commerce business, which is now 78.5% of revenue. Official H1FY27 filings show revenue up 113.7% YoY to ₹44,349 cr and PAT up 141.1% to ₹217 cr, but growth has slowed from +168.5% in FY26 and PAT margin has narrowed from 0.7% to 0.5%. Most of that revenue comes from Blinkit (₹34,816 cr, +183%) at only a 2.5% segment margin, while food delivery (+36.9%, 19.5% margin) still earns most of the profit, and Hyperpure (-34%) and Going Out (-18.7% margin) are a drag. Free cash flow was also negative at ₹-1,378 cr for H1. On valuation, P/E is not a useful yardstick for a platform like this, so I used EV/sales, growth delivery and unit economics. On those terms, 4.2× sales on revenue earning roughly 4–5% EBITDA, an EV/EBITDA of about 193× and a forward P/E of 61× (the most expensive of 20 sector peers, P100) grade it as expensive. The biggest risk is that the business has not yet shown it can reach Blinkit's long-term 4–6% margin target while competition stays intense: analysts have cut current-year EPS estimates by 35% in 30 days even though 29 of 32 still rate it a buy, which is a classic pattern before a stock de-rates.

fundamental.thesis: Avenue Supermarts (DMART) is India's dominant value-format grocery retailer (~500 stores, FY26) built on an everyday-low-price model with best-in-class inventory turnover (4.93× for H1FY27), giving it durable structural advantages in organised grocery. H1FY27 revenue grew +16.4% YoY to ₹38,439 cr (steady within a consistent +13–16% band over six periods), but PAT grew only +10.0% to ₹1,603 cr as PAT margin contracted to 4.17% from 4.4% — finance costs surged 84% to fund aggressive expansion, the Avenue E-commerce subsidiary dragged ₹166.62 cr in losses, and CFO/PAT collapsed from 0.96× (H1FY26) to 0.34× (H1FY27), signalling a meaningful deterioration in earnings quality. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary valuation yardstick (capital-intensive retail with PAT margins distorted by lease and e-commerce costs), DMART trades at 52.4× EV/EBITDA — P100 (most expensive) among 13 Consumer Discr. peers and +51% above the sector median — while trailing P/E of 89.1× is also P100 and +73% above sector median; sell-side EPS estimates have been revised down -3.1% over 90 days, a textbook pre-derating signal. The biggest risk is that the quick-commerce threat from Blinkit erodes SSSG momentum just as e-commerce losses widen and leverage builds, triggering the 25–40% multiple reset the sector card explicitly flags for any guidance disappointment at these premium valuations.

Shriram Finance is India's largest used commercial-vehicle financier, a diversified retail NBFC that also lends to small businesses, gold-loan and two-wheeler borrowers. Q2FY27, worked out as H1FY27 minus Q1FY27, shows total income of about ₹13,774 cr (+15.6% YoY) and PAT of about ₹3,684 cr (+59% YoY). Revenue growth has been steady at around +16% but is slowing from +19% in FY26, and AUM growth has eased to about 14.9%. Much of the PAT jump and the margin rise to about 26.7% comes from MUFG's ₹39,618 cr equity investment, which cut borrowing needs. That deal also added about 25% more shares, so per-share earnings grew about +28%, not 59%. We value NBFCs on price-to-book against return on equity, as the sector card says to, not on P/E. At 2.56× book with a 16.4% ROE, the stock is at the P33 of its peer group and 16% below the peer median of 3.0×. Trailing P/E is 16.8× and forward P/E is 12.9×. That makes it fair, leaning cheap. The new capital will push ROE down in the near term, which limits how far the valuation can re-rate. The main risk is asset quality: gross NPA (bad loans as a share of all loans) has edged up from 4.54% to 4.65%, and loan-loss charges rose 27.5% YoY, faster than the loan book, while crude above $100 squeezes the truck operators who are its core borrowers.

On P/B + ROE, the stock trades at 1.5x book with TTM ROE of 12.6% — sitting at the cheap-to-fair boundary per sector card guidelines (P/B < 1.5x with ROE > 12% = cheap), and trailing P/E of 11.4x is 34.8% below the Financials sector median of 17.5x (P33 peer rank), grading as fair overall. Havells is a leading Indian maker of electrical goods: switchgear, cables and wires, lighting, fans and appliances, plus Lloyd air conditioners. Its switchgear franchise is very profitable, with a 38.1% segment margin. Quarterly revenue growth has sped up from +14.3% (Q3FY26) to +19.5% (Q1FY27) to +34.6% in Q2FY27, reaching ₹6,417 cr. Profit has not kept up: PAT rose only 11.4% to ₹353 cr, PAT margin fell from about 6.6% to 5.5% a year earlier, contribution margin dropped from 20.1% to 18.2%, cables margin fell from 17.7% to 13.9% on aluminium costs, and H1 PAT is down 4% even though revenue is up 26.5%. Some of that weakness comes from last year's base, which included a one-off ₹45 cr gain from a land sale. On valuation I used P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers. A trailing P/E of 42.4x is 21% below the peer median of 53.8x (P31), while forward P/E of 33.5x and EV/EBITDA of 33.1x sit close to the median (P41–P47). With the stock near its 52-week low, that makes it fair rather than cheap, especially as analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by about 5% over the last 30 days. The biggest worry is earnings quality. Operating cash flow was negative in Q2 (-0.45x of PAT, free cash flow about -₹814 cr) because of a cables inventory build and capex rising to ₹1,400 cr. Lloyd is still loss-making, the President resigned on 27 Oct, and crude and the risk-off market add further headwinds.

Recent orders worth ₹533–1,011 cr kept coming through October. In Q1FY27 revenue rose 24.9% YoY to ₹5,547 cr, but PAT rose only 8.8% to ₹1,055 cr, so PAT margin fell to 19.0% from about 22% in recent periods. Revenue growth is speeding up while margins shrink, and cash conversion was weak at 0.05x CFO/PAT in H1FY26. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card names for this business. At 36.0x against a peer median of 34.0x (P65), with trailing P/E of 49.8x (P44) and forward P/E of 36.3x, the stock looks fair relative to peers. It sits mid-range at 41% of its 52-week band, while sell-side estimates have drifted down slightly (-1.0% for next FY over 90 days). The biggest near-term risk is the Q2FY27 results due on 30 Oct: a third quarter of margin slippage, or weak cash conversion, could de-rate a stock priced for steady execution, in a RISK_OFF regime that is already a headwind for Industrials.

fundamental.thesis: PFC is India's largest government-owned infrastructure finance NBFC, the apex lender to the power sector (generation, transmission, distribution) and parent of REC Limited, with a combined consolidated AUM of ~₹10L+ cr — a proposed merger (PFC absorbs REC at 88:100, effective April 2027) would make it one of Asia's largest infrastructure lenders. Q1FY27 revenue was essentially flat at −0.04% YoY (₹28,527 cr) with PAT barely moving at +0.18% YoY (₹8,998 cr, 31.5% margin), loan book growth of only 7% YoY, and rising forex losses (₹837 cr vs ₹706 cr prior year) — a sharp deceleration from Q4/FY26's 16% PAT growth and a clear single-quarter slowdown, though CFO/PAT of 1.81x confirms earnings quality remains cash-backed. Using P/B + ROE — the correct yardstick per sector card for lenders — PFC at 1.08x P/B with 20.5% ROE is unambiguously cheap (threshold: P/B < 1.5 + ROE > 12% = cheap), and is ranked P0 (cheapest in peer group) on both P/B (1.1x vs sector median 3.0x) and trailing P/E (5.6x vs sector median 20.1x); asset quality is exceptional with GNPA 0.66% and net NPA 0.13%. The primary risk is that forward P/E (6.7x) exceeds trailing P/E (5.6x) — a market signal that earnings are expected to decline — compounded by PFC-REC merger integration complexity and EPS dilution risk from the 88:100 exchange ratio, all set against a RISK_OFF macro regime with sustained FII outflows (−₹41,850 cr 30-day net) that create a structural re-rating headwind for PSU financials.

fundamental.thesis: LIC is India's dominant PSU life insurer (roughly 60% market share by first-year premium) with an unrivalled agency distribution franchise of ~1.3 million agents and an implicit government guarantee on policyholder liabilities — a structural moat no private peer can replicate at comparable scale. The latest clean data (H1FY26) shows PAT growth accelerating to +15.3% YoY (₹21,056 cr) while revenue grew a more modest +4.8% YoY (₹215,780 cr), implying margin expansion; the prior solo quarter (Q1FY26) showed PAT growth of only +5.0%, so the direction of PAT improvement is positive — but only two periods have complete data, preventing a robust multi-quarter trajectory call, and CFO/PAT of 0.70× in H1FY26 is below the 0.60 concern threshold only narrowly, suggesting earnings quality is acceptable but not pristine. The correct valuation yardstick for a life insurer is P/EV (Price-to-Embedded Value), which is unavailable here; using the next-best available proxy — P/B of 2.05× against a TTM ROE of 42.4% — LIC is unambiguously cheap on any reasonable framework, and the peer comparison reinforces this: LICI sits at P0 (absolute cheapest in its peer group) on trailing P/E, forward P/E, P/B, and EV/EBITDA simultaneously, trading at an -83.8% discount to the sector median P/E — a discount partly structural (PSU status, legacy product mix, government-directed social mandates) but appearing excessive in magnitude against a business generating 42% ROE. The single biggest near-term risk is management continuity: MD Dinesh Pant's government-approved voluntary retirement was announced on 25 Sep 2026, and in a PSU insurer context, leadership transitions can disrupt ongoing product mix improvement, agency productivity initiatives, and investor-relations momentum heading into Q2FY27 results.

Lodha (Macrotech) is a large branded residential developer focused on Mumbai and Pune, and it is also monetising its Palava land bank, including a recent sale of data-centre land to Digital Edge. Following the sector card, I judge it on operating metrics rather than reported P&L. Pre-sales rose about 16% from ₹17,630 cr in FY25 to ₹20,500 cr in FY26, and FY27 guidance of ₹24,000 cr implies about 17%; Q1FY27 bookings were ₹4,629 cr, with ₹5,000 cr+ guided for Q2. Reported Q1FY27 revenue of ₹4,997 cr (+43% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,373 cr (+100%) look flattered by the land sale, and management declined to raise its FY27 PAT guidance of about ₹4,100 cr. Net debt fell ₹446 cr to ₹4,931 cr and Q1 collections grew 46% to ₹4,205 cr, but FY26 cash conversion was weak at 0.28x CFO/PAT. Using EV/pre-sales and P/B with ROE as the yardsticks, valuation is fair rather than cheap. Market cap is about 4.4x FY26 pre-sales and about 3.8x FY27 guided pre-sales, P/B is 3.9x against ROE of 15.7%, EV/EBITDA is 19.1x (P38 vs the broad market), and the stock sits at 29% of its 52-week range. The biggest near-term risk is Q2 results due 30 Oct 2026: H1 pre-sales are expected to land at only 40–42% of the full-year target, so a miss on pre-sales or collections would undercut the whole thesis in a risk-off, real-estate-underweight tape.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Power is India's largest private thermal power producer, with 18.3 GW operating, 95% of capacity tied up in long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) and a target of 42–45 GW by FY32. In Q2 FY27 revenue grew 28.5% YoY to ₹17,528 cr, slower than Q1's +33.9%. Reported PAT rose 141.5% to ₹7,019 cr, but ₹2,422 cr of that is one-time recovery of old customer dues; without it, PAT is roughly ₹4,600 cr, a margin of about 26% (assuming the full amount flows to profit). EBITDA margin fell from 44.3% to 36.1% quarter-on-quarter, and underlying EBITDA grew only 18.5% because fuel costs rose 41.8% and merchant volumes fell 43%, even though the per-unit tariff was higher. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive power producer: at 25.2x it is about 118% above the utilities peer median of 11.6x, and trailing P/E of 35.4x is far above the 10–18x utilities band, so the stock is expensive. With the price at 86% of its 52-week range, the market is already pricing in flawless delivery of the expansion plan. The biggest risk is that headline profit is flattered by one-off recoveries while the ₹2 trillion thermal build-out has to be funded and executed.

fundamental.thesis: REC is a state-owned lender that funds power and infrastructure projects. It is one of India's largest infra NBFCs and is moving through a pending merger into Power Finance Corporation (NSE/BSE no-objection letters received on 2026-10-19). Growth has turned negative: H1 FY27 total income was ₹29,435 cr (-1.8% YoY) and PAT was ₹7,670 cr (-11.6% YoY, from ₹8,681 cr). Revenue growth slowed steadily from +11.8% in H1FY26 to +9.5%, then +5.8%, then -1.8%, and PAT margin fell from 29.8% to 26.1% over the same stretch. Asset quality was improving as of 9MFY26 (gross NPA 0.88%, down from 1.06%; net NPA 0.20%; capital adequacy 24.3%), but loan growth was only 2.7% YoY at last report. For a lender the right yardstick is price-to-book against return on equity. On that basis the stock looks cheap: P/B of 1.09x with a 20% ROE, a trailing P/E of 5.6x against a peer median of 20.1x, and a ranking in the cheapest ~11% of its credit-services peers, with only PFC cheaper. Analysts have cut FY-EPS estimates by about 10% and next-year estimates by about 12–13% over 30–90 days. That suggests the market is pricing in lower earnings rather than mispricing the stock. The biggest risks are a weak swap ratio or messy terms in the PFC merger and continued shrinking of loan growth and margins.

fundamental.thesis: TVS Motor is India's third-largest two-wheeler maker and is gaining share across motorcycles, scooters, three-wheelers and EVs, while also running a growing financial-services arm. In Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38.6% YoY to ₹19,474 cr, up from +33.4% in Q1, and PAT rose 50.2% to ₹1,219 cr, slower than +64.4% in Q1; group volumes grew 27% to 1.92M units, EV two-wheelers grew 133% to 186k and international volumes grew 35%, but the EBITDA margin fell 53bps YoY to 14.5%. Valuation is expensive whichever measure you use: trailing P/E of 52.1x is well above the 18–30x OEM band and highest among peers (P100, +92% vs the 27.1x median), forward P/E is 30.1x, and EV/EBITDA is 22.5x (P83, +23% vs the 18.3x median); some snapshot fields look wrong (35% dividend yield, D/E of 306 that includes the lending arm, and a mean target that doesn't fit the 52-week range), so I gave those fields little weight. The main risk is earnings quality: CFO/PAT was only 0.29x and FCF was -₹1,945 cr in Q2, while net debt rose from ₹2,159 cr to ₹3,470 cr as the finance arm lent more and working capital absorbed cash, and the stock is priced for perfection while the macro backdrop is risk-off with crude above $100.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Green is India's largest renewable power producer (20,763 MW operational, up 24% YoY, plus the largest battery-storage installation in the country at Khavda), and it earns money by adding capacity and selling power under 25-year fixed-tariff contracts. Growth is real: H1FY27 revenue was ₹8,689 cr (+27.6% YoY) and PAT was ₹1,730 cr (+17.8% YoY, 19.9% margin), driven by energy sales rising 32%. However, the pre-computed 'accelerating' label mixes half-year, quarter and full-year periods, so it overstates the trend. The implied Q2 revenue (about ₹4,258 cr) was below Q1's ₹4,431 cr, and PAT is growing more slowly than revenue because interest and depreciation from the capex build eat into the gains. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-heavy IPP. At 31.8× against a utilities peer median of 11.6× (P100 in sector), and P/B of 12.7× on an ROE of only 7.6%, the stock is clearly expensive. It also trades at 94% of its 52-week range while sell-side FY EPS estimates have been cut 14.5% over 90 days. The biggest risk is the balance sheet: net debt is 5.6× EBITDA on ₹1.12 lakh cr of gross debt, and FCF was -₹7,141 cr in H1. That leaves the equity highly sensitive to interest rates in a weak-rupee, 5% US-yield world, and to any slip in commissioning, which is already exposed by the transmission Phase 3 delay and curtailment.

fundamental.thesis: M&M is India's dominant auto-farm conglomerate holding #1 positions across SUVs (25.3% share, +260 bps YoY), LCVs (52.3%), tractors (43.6%), and e-3-wheelers (40%), with further exposure to financial services (MMFSL), IT (TechM), real estate, and hospitality — a diversified conglomerate structure that blends cyclical and defensive earnings. Q1 FY27 delivered consolidated revenue of ₹58,188 cr (+27.8% YoY) and PAT of ₹5,455 cr (+33.6% YoY), sustaining a remarkably consistent multi-quarter growth corridor of +25–28% revenue and +33–37% PAT, with PAT margins expanding from 8.6% (FY26) to 9.4% (Q1 FY27); guidance raised twice and then maintained once signals management confidence is intact. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick (appropriate for a capital-intensive OEM with a large NBFC subsidiary), M&M trades at 10.7× vs the sector peer median of 18.3×, ranking at P17 in its peer set — unambiguously cheap; trailing P/E of 19.5× is also at the lower quartile of the 18–28× Auto OEM sector range (P20 vs peers), though the stock sits at only 15.5% of its 52-week range, signalling downward momentum that could persist before fundamentals reassert. fundamental.thesis: Canara Bank is India's third-largest public-sector bank (PSB) by advances (~₹13.6L cr loan book), with ~63% GoI ownership, a broad retail network, and significant corporate/wholesale banking exposure. H1FY27 PAT surged +31.3% YoY to ₹10,562 cr — a strong profit trajectory — despite total income contracting -3.4% YoY to ₹80,635 cr, driven by NPA recovery write-backs and sharply improved asset quality (Gross NPA down to 1.33% vs 1.84% in Q4FY26, Net NPA at 0.30% with PCR of 95.34%); loan growth accelerated to +19% YoY, while PAT margin expanded from 11.7% (FY26) to 13.1% (H1FY27) — the direction of margin improvement is the key positive signal even as top-line revenue is under pressure from NIM compression and treasury losses. At P/B of 1.02× against ROE of 15.9%, CANBK is deeply cheap by the P/B+ROE yardstick appropriate for lenders — sector card explicitly calls P/B vs sustainable ROE as the correct valuation lens; the stock sits at P0 (cheapest in its 14-peer peer group) on both trailing P/E (6.1× vs median 16.8×) and forward P/E (5.7×), and at P21 on P/B (1.0× vs median 1.5×), representing a substantial discount to peers that appears only partially explained by PSB quality discount. The single biggest risk is NIM compression continuing — NIM was 2.06% (FY26 blended) vs the 2.51% sequential figure, and with EBLR-linked loans repricing down in a rate-cut cycle and CASA ratio structurally weak at ~29.9%, any further compression in net interest spread would suppress top-line recovery and challenge the PAT margin expansion story.

Info Edge runs Naukri, India's dominant online recruitment platform, plus 99acres in real estate and Jeevansathi/Shiksha, and holds large stakes in listed and unlisted startups that make up much of its book value. Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹756 cr (+120% YoY, an 87% margin) is almost certainly inflated by one-off investment gains, so it should not be read as core profitability. Core recruitment margin was ~55% in the last segment data, real estate is still loss-making (₹5.9 cr loss), and the business has negligible borrowings, though the extracted figures are internally inconsistent. On valuation, I used EV/EBITDA plus peer-relative P/E, per the sector card's platform yardstick. Trailing P/E of 44.7x looks cheap against the Consumer Discr. peer median of 79x (P22), but EV/EBITDA of 53x sits above the 48x median (P78), and the low 1.33x P/B and 4.6% ROE are distorted by the investment portfolio. The biggest risk is the Q2 FY27 result due 28 Oct: a further slowdown in hiring-driven billings, especially from IT services clients, would confirm deceleration, while sell-side estimates are already flat to slightly lower over 90 days.

fundamental.thesis: Marico is a leading Indian FMCG company with dominant franchises in hair oils (Parachute) and branded health foods (Saffola), holding strong distribution in both rural and urban India alongside a growing international business. Indian Hotels (IHCL, owner of the Taj brand) is India's largest hospitality company, with 670 hotels in its portfolio, 390 of them operating and 280 in the pipeline. Its management-fee and select-service businesses are each growing about 25%. In Q2FY27 consolidated revenue rose 21.0% YoY to ₹2,566 cr, speeding up from +14.6% in Q1FY27, and PAT rose 23.0% to ₹349 cr. RevPAR grew 25% YoY, and management raised FY27 revenue guidance from 12-14% to 15-17%. The 'contracting' margin signal is mostly an artifact of comparing a seasonally weak monsoon quarter (13.6% PAT margin, 30.7% EBITDA margin) against full-year FY26 figures; EBITDA grew 21%, in line with revenue, so year-on-year margins look roughly flat to slightly up. Cash conversion is solid: H1 CFO/PAT is 1.27x, H1 free cash flow is ₹546 cr, and the company holds ₹4,369 cr of gross cash. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for a capital-intensive hotel business, the stock trades at 28.2x versus a sector median of 21.9x (P61). That premium is justified by an upswing in the RevPAR cycle, a forward P/E of 35.6x versus 44.5x trailing, upward earnings-estimate revisions, and a mid-range 52-week position (38.5%), so I grade it fair rather than cheap. The main threat to this view is a slowdown in discretionary travel and events demand in a risk-off, high-crude macro backdrop, which could force a guidance reset on a stock priced at a premium multiple.

Revenue growth has firmed from +14.3% to about +18% over five periods, while PAT margin has held flat at about 23%. Beneath that, net interest income grew only 9.8% YoY in H1 against 25% AUM growth, NIM has slipped from 3.5% to 3.36%, credit cost rose to 0.52% in Q1FY27 from 0.05–0.20% earlier, and capital adequacy fell from 26.1% to 21.2% as leverage climbed to 4.9x debt/equity. Using P/B against ROE (the right yardstick for a lender), 3.19x book for a 12.1–12.6% ROE is expensive, and trailing P/E of 28x sits at the top of the 18–28x NBFC band; forward P/E of 19.9x and the 25th-percentile 52-week position soften but do not overturn that verdict. The biggest risk is profit growth falling behind loan growth as margins thin and credit costs normalise, made worse by the CFO's resignation on 2026-10-23 and next-year earnings estimates being trimmed (-1.1% over 90 days).

Trailing P/E of 32.3× sits above the IT sector upper bound of 30× and is difficult to justify given the deceleration trajectory, contracting PAT margins, sell-side estimates cut 8.1% over 90 days, and a Debt/Equity of 1.86 that is unusually high for an asset-light analytics business; the stock is trading at 22.7% of its 52-week range, reflecting the market's scepticism, but the multiple compression needed to reach fair value has not fully run its course. The biggest risk is that the new CEO re-rates cost structure upward while discretionary analytics spend from US BFSI clients softens, trapping the stock in a simultaneous revenue deceleration and margin contraction cycle that drives a sustained EPS downgrade.

Trailing P/E of 23.65× sits within the IT sector benchmark range of 22–30×, grading FAIR; however, forward P/E of 17.21× falls significantly below the sector lower bound and the EV/EBITDA of 15.15× is at a 35% discount to the broad-market median (23.3×), and with the stock at just 7.4% of its 52-week range (near lows), risk/reward tilts incrementally toward cheap — primary yardstick used is P/E + EV/EBITDA given the IT services capital-light model. fundamental.thesis: C.E. Info Systems (MapMyIndia) is India's dominant digital mapping and location intelligence platform, holding a near-monopoly in B2B GIS/API/SaaS services with 83.5% of revenue from high-margin subscription-type map data; it competes with no listed domestic peer of comparable depth, giving it structural pricing power. Q1FY27 headline revenue grew +14.9% YoY to ₹139.72 cr (PAT ₹50 cr, +7.9% YoY, margin recovering to 35.6% from a 9MFY26 trough of 22.8%), but the acceleration is almost entirely device-driven (GPS/IoT +204% YoY to ₹23.11 cr) — the core mapping segment, which is the durable cash engine, grew only 2.28% YoY, a saturation signal that the headline masks. On valuation, trailing P/E of 36.88x sits above the IT sector median upper bound of 30x and EV/EBITDA of 29.08x is at P64 vs broad peers (+24.7% premium to median), but forward P/E of 22.49x (P48, a 39% discount to trailing) and the stock sitting at just 10.9% of its 52-week range (near ₹795 low vs ₹1,998 high) together grade this 'fair' rather than 'expensive' — the price has corrected more than fundamentals warrant, but the core-segment stall prevents a 'cheap' call. The biggest risk is that device revenue is lumpy, lower-margin, and non-recurring — if it fades, headline growth reverts to 2-3% core growth — and the September 2026 NSE volume-movement clarification request alongside a subsidiary director resignation introduces near-term governance uncertainty at a time when sell-side EPS estimates are being cut (90d Δ: −4.6% current FY, −6.5% next FY).

Netweb Technologies is a mid-cap Indian maker of high-performance computing, AI servers and private-cloud hardware. The desk's IT-services sector card fits it poorly, so this view leans on its own filings and on EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for a hardware business. The last reliable quarter, Q1 FY27, showed revenue of about ₹714 cr (yfinance shows ₹671 cr) and PAT of ₹85 cr, a 12.0% PAT margin. Both revenue and PAT more than doubled year-on-year, but the sources conflict on the exact rate (+137% from the table's own numbers vs +174.5% stated), and the H1 FY27 figures (₹2,143 cr revenue, ₹423 cr PAT, 19.7% margin) come from an OCR-corrupted filing and are not used. Reported order/deal value fell from ₹2,184 cr (H1 FY26) to ₹450 cr (Q3FY26), the latest point available, and EBITDA margin slipped from 14.9% to about 12–13%, so the growth looks real but lumpy. On valuation the stock is expensive: EV/EBITDA of 79.2× sits in the 96th percentile of the broad market, against a median of 23.3×, and trailing P/E of 108.7× (forward 60.7×) is far above any sector benchmark. That leaves little room for error if order inflow or margins disappoint in a risk-off, midcap-unfriendly market.

fundamental.thesis: Newgen Software is a mid-cap Indian enterprise software product company (low-code, digital process automation and the NewgenONE AI platform) selling mainly to banks, insurers and governments, with 63.5% of revenue now recurring (annuity). In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,032 cr (+22.5% YoY) and PAT ₹284 cr (+13.3% YoY), but revenue growth has slowed each period from +35.7% (Q3FY26) to +29.1% (FY26), +25.0% (H1FY27) and +22.5% now; constant-currency growth is only about 12.2%, so roughly half of the headline growth comes from the weaker rupee, and PAT margin fell to 14.0% from 15.1% a year ago, with adjusted PAT up just 8.1%. The biggest risks are heavy client concentration (top-3 clients are 60.1% of revenue, top-10 are 84.4%) together with slowing underlying growth and high attrition of 25.7%.

fundamental.thesis: Sonata Software is a mid-cap IT services company focused on platform-led modernisation (MASC stack) with growing cloud/AI partnerships — the September 2026 five-year AWS SCA signals enterprise positioning, and appointment of a Chief AI Officer suggests management repositioning toward AI-native delivery. The most alarming data point is that constant-currency revenue growth turned NEGATIVE at -2.4% in Q1FY26 even as reported INR revenue rose +17.3% YoY, exposing a rupee-depreciation veil over real volume pressure; PAT margin contracted from 4.2% (FY25) to 3.7% (Q1FY26) while FY25 PAT fell -12.1% YoY despite 17.9% revenue growth — a classic case of revenue growth masking margin destruction and PAT decline. At a trailing P/E of 15.57× against the IT sector median of 22–30×, the stock screens unambiguously cheap (P15 vs broad market, -55.7% vs median) and forward P/E of 12.69× implies the market has already priced in some earnings recovery — but the deep discount is likely deserved given negative CC growth, high debt/equity of 37.96, and 90-day EPS estimate cuts of -5.4% that signal sell-side conviction in the deterioration. The biggest fundamental risk is that AI-driven budget deflation in Sonata's enterprise client base makes negative CC growth structural rather than cyclical, converting apparent valuation cheapness into a sustained earnings-decline trap — data quality is further constrained by filing staleness (latest indexed extraction is 9M FY25, making Q1 FY27 performance unconfirmed from official sources).

fundamental.thesis: Tata Elxsi is a Tata Group engineering R&D services company specialising in embedded systems design for automotive, media & entertainment, and healthcare verticals — a niche deep-tech services player distinct from commodity IT outsourcers, with a strong domestic and global client base in high-complexity design programmes. Revenue growth has inflected sharply from a -3.9% trough in Q2FY26 to +14.7% YoY in H1FY27 (₹2,077 cr), with PAT rising +13.9% to ₹341 cr and PAT margin holding steady at 16.4%; the System Integration segment contributed 28.9% YoY growth, signalling service diversification — however, EBITDA margin has contracted ~290 bps from its peak of 28.1% (Q3FY26) to 25.2% (H1FY27), driven by New Labour Code wage provisions and rising employee benefits costs. Trailing P/E of 40.78× is above the IT sector benchmark upper bound of 30× (expensive on that metric alone), but the forward P/E collapses to 26.22× — within the 22–30× sector range, confirming earnings recovery is priced in — and peer-rank analysis places TATAELXSI at P60 on both trailing and forward P/E (fairly valued per the ≥P75 expensive threshold); at 6.7% of its 52-week range the stock appears sentiment-oversold relative to an improving earnings trajectory, consistent with the FY26 exceptional charge now cycling out of the base. The primary risk is sustained EBITDA margin compression from structural wage inflation and New Labour Code costs, amplified by a persistent negative EPS revision trend (-0.9% over 90 days, -1.2% next-FY) that historically flags further analyst downgrades ahead, and a long-run AI-driven structural threat to engineering services demand that the sector card explicitly flags as unproven in revenue terms.

Tata Technologies is a mid-cap engineering and R&D services firm focused on automotive, working with global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers on vehicle programs and software-defined vehicle work, and it now owns ES-Tec GmbH (acquired in FY26). Q2FY27 revenue rose 28.4% YoY to ₹1,699 cr, with services up 33.9%, and EBITDA margin improved 40 bps to 16.1%, but PAT grew only 3.6% to ₹171 cr and PAT margin fell 240 bps YoY to 10.1%. Much of the top-line jump likely comes from the ES-Tec acquisition rather than organic demand. Two further cautions: the pre-computed 'accelerating' label compares one quarter to a full year, and the yfinance quarterly revenue (₹1,274 cr) does not reconcile with the filings, so this is not a clean multi-quarter acceleration. On valuation (yardstick: trailing P/E plus EV/EBITDA for IT services), a trailing P/E of 56.0x is well above the 22–30x IT range, EV/EBITDA of 39.6x sits at P82 vs peers, and the stock is at 89% of its 52-week range. That makes it expensive even after crediting the lower 33.0x forward P/E. The biggest risk is that earnings fail to follow revenue: FY-EPS estimates have been cut 4.9% in 30 days, management flags near-term softness in certain customers and geographies, and the full-year 'strong double-digit growth' guidance has been maintained rather than raised.

fundamental.thesis: CESC is a regulated integrated power utility (generation + distribution + captive coal) serving the Kolkata/West Bengal circle under WBERC oversight, earning returns on a tariff-order framework supplemented by FPPA fuel pass-throughs and periodic regulatory income recognition. FY26 official filings (PDF, May 2026) show revenue of ₹18,570 cr (+9.2% YoY, decelerating from +10.2% in 9MFY25) and PAT of ₹1,542 cr (+12.5%), but Q1FY27 results (filed August 2026) remain unread, introducing a quarter-lag in the trajectory picture; the EBITDA margin contracted sharply from 24.4% in 9MFY25 to 15.7% in Q1FY26 before recovering to 19.1% for full-year FY26, signalling uneven cost absorption. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for a capital-intensive regulated utility, 10.92× is modest and the trailing P/E of 14.68× sits within the sector benchmark range of 10–18×; peer rank of P14 (bottom quartile vs 473 stocks, -58% discount to broad-market median P/E) and a forward P/E of 11.9× below trailing both point to cheap positioning, though the low ROE of 12.5% and high leverage limit re-rating potential. The central risk is financial leverage (D/E 1.7×, net debt 4.44× EBITDA, DSCR 1.2×, current ratio 0.9) in a rising-rate and weakening-INR environment, layered over unresolved APTEL appeals on tariff orders spanning FY2015–FY2026 that could force retroactive adjustments to recognised regulatory income.

Jaiprakash Power Ventures is a midcap private power producer (thermal plus the Vishnu Prayag hydro plant) whose former promoter group, Jaiprakash Associates, was taken over by Adani Enterprises through insolvency in March 2026; it does not fit the regulated-return model the Utilities sector card describes. The last quarter extracted from the official filings, Q1 FY27, shows revenue up 12.2% YoY to ₹1,776 cr and PAT up 68.5% to ₹469 cr. That jump follows a weak FY26 (revenue +1.9%, PAT -44.6%) and is distorted by a one-time ₹108 cr net tax benefit and a ₹194 cr coal-mine surrender provision. The Q2 FY27 results filed on 19 Oct are not yet in the trend table, and the unverified yfinance figures (PAT ₹33 cr) hint at a sharp seasonal or underlying drop, so the 'accelerating' trajectory label should not be trusted. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for this capital-heavy business, 11.4x (P16 vs the broad market) and P/B of 1.23x look reasonable, but trailing P/E of 22.9x is above the 10–18x utilities band, so overall it is fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is roughly ₹2,000 cr of disputed claims (UPPCL ₹473 cr, AP sand-mining notices ₹857 cr, ICICI recompense ₹570 cr, a ~₹124 cr JAL guarantee), about 18% of market cap and none provided for, made worse by the CFO and Company Secretary both leaving on 30 Sep 2026.

Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock trades at 8.12× vs the 9–12× India towerco norm — objectively cheap — and sits at P7 in the broad-market EV/EBITDA ranking and P15 on trailing P/E; forward P/E of 13.31× below trailing (15.29×) signals the market is pricing in an earnings recovery, while Operating FCF surged 23.4% YoY to ₹1,781 cr offering genuine cash-backing to that view. Urban Company is India's largest online platform for home services such as beauty, cleaning and repairs, and it also sells its own water purifiers and smart locks (Native), runs international operations and has a Saudi joint venture. It is now funding a heavily loss-making quick home-help business called InstaHelp. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹537 cr, up 41% YoY, faster than FY26's +36%. Orders rose 103% and Net Transaction Value (NTV, the total value of services booked) rose 39% to ₹1,432 cr. Profit went the other way: consolidated adjusted EBITDA was -₹144 cr, a -26.8% margin, against +6.8% for FY26. That is because InstaHelp lost ₹174 cr, which wiped out a core business that is profitable and improving (core EBITDA ₹30 cr, up 213% YoY; India consumer margin 3.5%, up 110 bps). Since the business is pre-profit, P/E means nothing here, so I graded valuation on price-to-sales and unit economics instead. At 12.3x sales and 8.6x book value (76th percentile of the broad market), the price is reasonable for 40% growth only if InstaHelp's losses keep shrinking. InstaHelp's loss per order did improve 19% from the previous quarter but is still ₹279. I rate valuation fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is that the InstaHelp cash burn continues while the newly approved ₹2,500 cr capital raise dilutes shareholders, in a risk-off market that punishes high-multiple loss-makers.

fundamental.thesis: CEAT is India's #4 tyre maker (global rank #4 by brand) with 51% replacement, 30% OEM, and 19% export mix, operating at 95% capacity utilisation across ~80,000 daily tyres — a capital-intensive ancillary with defensive replacement demand. Q2FY27 revenue grew a strong +26.2% YoY to ₹4,762 cr, but PAT collapsed -39.8% YoY to ₹112 cr as EBITDA margins contracted sharply from ~13–14% (FY26/Q3FY26) to just 9.5% today — this is the defining trajectory: top-line accelerating while margins are structurally compressing, driven by commodity cost headwinds from the West Asia conflict and the Camso acquisition integration costs; the DSCR of 0.84× (below the 1.0× sustainability floor) and a current ratio of 0.67× flag tightening liquidity. Valuation looks outright cheap: EV/EBITDA at 7.4× sits at P5 vs the broad market (median 23.3×), trailing P/E of 20.2× is at P23 vs peers and -43% below market median — using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock screens as cheap, but the multiple compression is warranted given the margin collapse, and forward P/E of 15.1× implies the market expects earnings recovery, which is far from assured. The single biggest risk is that commodity costs (natural rubber, crude derivatives) persist or worsen into H2FY27, keeping EBITDA margins pinned at 9–10% and preventing the earnings recovery the forward P/E demands — a second consecutive quarter of PAT decline would trigger a meaningful derating.

CIE Automotive India makes forged, cast and machined components for auto OEMs, with about two-thirds of revenue from India and the rest from Europe (it reports on a calendar year, so 9M26 means Jan–Sep 2026). Revenue for 9M26 rose 12.1% YoY to ₹7,866 cr and PAT rose 16.8% to ₹729 cr. India grew 14.7% while Europe grew only 7.4%. Growth is steady but edging down: from +13.0% in H1 to +12.1% for 9M, which implies about +10% in Q3 on its own. EBITDA margin also slipped from 16.7% in H1 to 16.1% for 9M. I graded valuation on P/E, the yardstick the sector card uses for auto names. Trailing P/E is 20.0x, in the lower half of the sector's 18–30x band, and forward P/E is 15.9x, so the market expects earnings to grow. EV/EBITDA is 18.9x against a broad-market median of 23.3x. That makes the stock fair, leaning cheap, but the peer ranking (P22 on P/E) compares it with the whole market, not auto peers, so I put less weight on it. The main risks are weak cash conversion (H1 free cash flow was -₹263 cr, with operating cash flow at -0.04x PAT) and a slow Europe business. Analysts keep cutting estimates (FY EPS down 2.3% over 90 days) even though 4 of 5 rate it a buy, and rising crude in a risk-off market is a headwind for auto demand.

At 27.85× trailing P/E — FAIR for a specialty agrochem franchise (sector-appropriate range 25–40×; stock at P37 in broad-market P/E ranking, 21% discount to 35.2× median) with forward P/E of 21.76× signalling expected earnings recovery — the multiple is not stretched, but the stock trading at just 3% above its 52-week low combined with analyst next-FY EPS revisions trending negative (−2.8% over 90 days) blurs whether this is value entry or falling knife. The primary risk is a prolonged agrochem demand trough from recurring monsoon disruptions and China-price-war realisation compression, compounded by an unusually high D/E of 2.76 and ₹3,500 cr in approved FY28 related-party transactions with Bayer AG creating governance and cash-flow unpredictability in a RISK_OFF macro regime.

fundamental.thesis: FACT is a PSU fertilizer producer (primarily complex fertilizers under the FACTAMFOS brand) operating as a near-monopoly in Kerala/South India, heavily dependent on government subsidy disbursements and imported raw materials — a price-taker in both inputs and outputs. Revenue recovered sharply to ₹1,484 cr in Q1 FY27 (+41.9% YoY, accelerating from the -24.9% trough of 9M FY2025), but this top-line bounce has not translated into operating profits: the fertilizer segment PBIT margin sits at -1.86%, the Q1 FY27 operating loss before finance costs was ₹36.51 cr, and the headline PAT of ₹3 cr (0.21% margin) is a statistical artefact of non-operating income rather than genuine operational recovery — full-year FY26 PAT was -₹40 cr. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per the sector card), FACT trades at 120.63× vs a fertilizer/chemicals cyclical mid-cycle norm of 5–8×, ranks P99 among 403 broad-market peers, and carries a P/B of 36.81× on a near-zero ROE — this is unambiguously expensive; the ₹50,886 cr market cap is disconnected from any demonstrated earnings power. The single largest risk is the compounding of a post-Q1 raw-material supply shock (West Asia geopolitical disruptions already causing plant shutdowns) on top of extreme financial leverage (D/E 295×) where quarterly finance costs of ₹61.98 cr structurally exceed operating income, leaving zero buffer for further stress.

fundamental.thesis: Gujarat Fluorochemicals is India's dominant integrated fluorochemical and fluoropolymer producer — holding a near-monopoly in domestic ref-gas (R32, R134A) and fluoropolymers — now executing a high-stakes diversification into EV battery materials via its GFCL EV subsidiary. Q1FY27 revenue of ₹1,588 cr grew +24% YoY with EBITDA expanding 24% to ₹428 cr (27% margin) and PAT +20% YoY to ₹219 cr (14% margin), representing a sharp re-acceleration from the -1.1% revenue trough in Q3FY26, driven by a fluorochemicals surge of +52% YoY; the PAT margin trajectory remains mixed however — recovering from Q4FY26's 8.2% trough but still below the 14.6% achieved in H1FY26, and the trajectory signal flags structural compression as the loss-making battery materials drag deepens (GFCL EV EBITDA -144% on ₹14 cr revenue in Q1FY27). Valuation is unambiguously expensive using EV/EBITDA — the primary yardstick for capital-intensive specialty chemicals — at 42.17×, a level that far exceeds even premium Indian specialty chemical peers trading at 20–30×, and is well above the 5–8× mid-cycle benchmark for commodity chemicals; the stock sits at 91.5% of its 52-week range and consensus estimate revisions are running -5.4% on a 90-day basis, a classic pre-derating signal. The central risk is execution on a ₹6,000 cr capex commitment by FY28 for a segment (battery materials) that posted a ₹30 cr EBITDA loss on ₹14 cr revenue in the latest quarter, compounding an already negative FY26 FCF of ₹-291 cr and high reported leverage.

fundamental.thesis: GMDCLTD is a Gujarat state-government PSU primarily engaged in lignite mining (92% of segment revenue) with a structurally loss-making power segment; it is a commodity cyclical where EV/EBITDA — not P/E — is the correct yardstick per the sector card. Q1FY27 showed a revenue recovery to ₹907 cr (+23.8% YoY) driven by mining (+22.7% to ₹841 cr), but PAT was essentially flat at ₹163 cr (-0.2% YoY), with PAT margin compressing sharply from FY26's elevated 36% to 18% — operating leverage destroyed by a 13-fold surge in finance costs (₹6.61 cr vs ₹0.51 cr YoY) and the power segment swinging to a ₹6 cr operating loss from a ₹10.6 cr profit. At EV/EBITDA of 43.9× (P85 vs 473 broad-market peers, +88% premium to the median 23.3×), the stock is expensive on its primary capital-intensive multiple despite a superficially cheap trailing P/E of 20.6× (P23) — the P/E is optically cheap because ₹324 cr in FY26 non-operating interest/dividend income inflates PAT well above operating earnings, a persistent distortion for this PSU. The biggest risk is the structural squeeze: negative FCF (−₹290 cr FY26), a capex/revenue ratio of 39%, rapidly rising debt-servicing costs, and a power segment with a −36.9% operating margin in FY26 that shows no credible path to profitability.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Copper (HINDCOPPER) is India's only vertically integrated copper mining and smelting PSU, with a near-monopoly on domestic copper ore mining and implicit government backing as a strategic-metal producer. Q1FY27 delivered revenue of ₹936cr (+81.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹352cr (+162.5% YoY), with PAT margin expanding sharply to 37.6% from 26.0% a year ago and EBITDA margin surging to 56%; growth has clearly accelerated from a muted +4.6% YoY in Q1FY26, driven overwhelmingly by higher copper realisations rather than volume — a commodity-price-lift story, not a structural earnings re-rating. Using EV/EBITDA as the correct yardstick for a capital-intensive commodity cyclical (per sector card), HINDCOPPER trades at 33.4× — more than 4× the mid-cycle cyclical benchmark of 5–8× and +43% above the broad-market median (P70); trailing P/E of 53.5× is also far above the Materials sector range of 12–22×, grading the stock as expensive. The critical risk is that copper-price cyclicality combined with high financial leverage (D/E 3.32), negative FY26 FCF (-₹182cr), a thin analyst base (1 analyst), and the absence of management guidance creates severe downside asymmetry if LME copper prices correct or China demand weakens — macro headwinds (risk-off, rising crude, weakening INR) compound this.

fundamental.thesis: Hindustan Zinc is India's dominant integrated zinc-lead-silver miner (Vedanta Group subsidiary) with near-monopoly status in domestic mined zinc and structural cost advantages that produce world-class EBITDA margins of 62.4% — a level no domestic peer can match. H1FY27 revenue surged 76.7% YoY to ₹28,840 cr (accelerating sharply from -4.4% in Q1FY26), PAT grew 143.4% YoY to ₹11,881 cr, and PAT margin expanded to 41.2% from 29.9% — a five-period trajectory of simultaneously accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins driven primarily by elevated zinc and silver commodity prices, with cash quality strong (CFO/PAT 1.12×). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive commodity miner, the stock trades at 10.59× — P13 among 473 peers and a 54.6% discount to the broad-market EV/EBITDA median — with trailing P/E of 17.46× squarely inside the Materials sector range (12–22×), grading cheap on peer-relative metrics, though 10.59× sits above the 5–8× typical mid-cycle range for base-metals cyclicals, signalling that some commodity-cycle-peak risk remains unpriced. The thesis is materially constrained by an unresolved ED/FEMA investigation (search and seizure June 2026, no regulatory communication as of the October 2026 filing) and SEBI observations on related party transaction disclosures — governance headwinds typical of Vedanta Group that can trigger a de-rating independent of commodity fundamentals, and are weighted heavily under the midcap governance overlay.

fundamental.thesis: Linde India is the Indian subsidiary of Linde plc, operating in industrial gases (on-site, merchant, packaged supply) and project engineering for gas plants — a quasi-utility business with long-term supply contracts and high barriers to entry. Q1FY27 revenue grew a strong +21.6% YoY to ₹694 cr driven by the gases segment (+8.9% to ₹544 cr), but PAT declined 2.4% YoY to ₹104.6 cr on a 10.9% jump in tax expense, and EBITDA margin has contracted from 44.5% to 30.0% over the last four reported periods — a consistent compression trend that is the primary fundamental concern. At a trailing P/E of 99.6× versus the Materials sector median of 12–22×, the stock is unambiguously expensive; even granting an industrial-gases premium for quasi-utility earnings quality, the stock ranks at P93 on trailing P/E and P98 on forward P/E versus 473 broad-market peers, with EPS estimates cut 13–14% over the last 90 days — a pre-derating pattern. The single biggest risk is the active SEBI investigation into material related party transactions with Praxair India Private Limited, compounded by an auditor qualified opinion on business allocation valuation and a Supreme Court case still pending — governance uncertainty of this nature is disqualifying for a position-sizing decision at current valuations.

fundamental.thesis: NMDC is India's largest iron ore producer — a Navratna PSU with near-monopoly domestic supply position — operating exclusively in iron ore mining and pelletisation after the demerger of NMDC Steel Limited in FY24; its cost advantage and long-term customer agreements provide a durable business moat. Q1FY27 revenue grew just +0.8% YoY (₹6,795 cr), a sharp deceleration from the +27–33% range seen across FY26 and H1FY26, but EBITDA surged 23.3% YoY to ₹3,190 cr on 854 bps of margin expansion to 46.9%, and PAT held at ₹1,976 cr (+0.4% YoY, 29.1% margin) — the revenue line has stalled while operational leverage has sharply improved. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary multiple per sector card guidance for capital-intensive commodity names, NMDC trades at 7.81×, within the 5–8× mid-cycle commodity range and at P6 (cheapest 6%) vs 473 broader-market peers; trailing P/E of 10.45× sits below the 12–22× Materials sector lower bound — graded cheap, though the EV/EBITDA at the top of the mid-cycle range limits the cheapness margin. The dominant overhang is the ₹15,785.72 cr Karnataka Mineral Rights Tax contingent liability (≈20% of market cap), awaiting Presidential assent, combined with ₹11+ cr of stressed receivables from demerged NSL and government-owned RINL that depressed CFO/PAT cash conversion to 0.66× in FY26.

fundamental.thesis: NMDC Steel is a government-controlled (50.79% GoI stake) integrated steel producer demerged from NMDC Ltd, operating a greenfield Nagarnar plant and currently awaiting a strategic disinvestment buyer — creating a persistent ownership overhang. Q1FY27 revenue grew 8.8% YoY to ₹3,662cr, a sharp deceleration from +72.4% in 9MFY26 and +178.9% in FY25, but the critical directional story is the margin turnaround: PAT margin has expanded from −35.8% (Q3FY25) through −3.4% (9MFY26) to +1.4% (Q1FY27) as the greenfield plant ramps utilisation and fixed-cost absorption improves. Using EV/EBITDA — the correct yardstick for a capital-intensive steel cyclical — NSLNISP trades at 11.69× versus the broad-market median of 23.3×, placing it at P17 (cheap), and P/B of 1.05× puts it at P3; the 235× trailing P/E is a pure distortion of near-zero earnings and must not be read as 'expensive', but D/E of 35× and a DSCR of only 0.17 mean the company cannot comfortably service its own debt and any spread compression could tip it back to losses. The single biggest risk is that extreme financial leverage leaves no margin of safety against rising crude costs (a direct input-cost headwind in the current macro), a weakening rupee, and the prolonged disinvestment uncertainty that suppresses any rerating.

fundamental.thesis: Ramco Cements is a South India-focused cement producer (~6.1 MT capacity, ~73% utilisation in Q3FY26) operating in a sector undergoing consolidation. Q1FY27 revenues grew +9.6% YoY to ₹2,280 cr, but core operating profit before exceptional items collapsed 76% (₹114.87 cr → ₹27.77 cr), PAT fell 63% to ₹31.24 cr — and stripping the ₹12.62 cr land-sale gain, underlying PAT was only ₹18.62 cr; the critical cement KPI, EBITDA/tonne, has deteriorated sharply from ₹981 (Q1FY26) to ₹866 (Q2FY26) to ₹651 (Q3FY26) — well below the sector-healthy ₹900–1,100 range — suggesting cost inflation and/or pricing weakness are structurally outpacing volume gains. Valuation yardstick is EV/EBITDA (capital-intensive cement per sector card): EV/EBITDA of 17.05× sits inside the Materials benchmark (12–22×) suggesting fair pricing, but the EBITDA base is severely compressed and PAT quality is poor (exceptional land sales contribute the majority of reported profit), making the multiple misleading; sell-side has cut FY-EPS estimates −18.2% in 90 days with 12 sells vs 9 buys, reinforcing a pre-derating pattern. Biggest risk is that EBITDA/tonne stays depressed well into FY27 as rising crude/energy costs and muted regional cement pricing persist, leaving the stock at 13.8% of its 52-week range as a potential falling knife rather than a value entry.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
